terms.gloss: a flooding of the land by the sea, a tsunami
evidence: Plin. NH 2.200: fīunt simul cum terrae mōtū et inundātiōnēs maris
terms.comment: Pliny’s phrase for the sea that floods the land together with an earthquake, which is what a tsunami is. Ammianus Marcellinus (26.10) describes the great one of AD 365 at length, in late Latin. Morgan–Owens also lists modern coinages (aestus sīsmicus) and, after the poets, agger aquae.

terms.gloss: a mountain of water, a huge wave
terms.comment: Vergil’s picture of a storm wave rising over the ships; good for the wave itself, as a child sees it.

phrases.latin: Fīunt simul cum terrae mōtū et inundātiōnēs maris.
phrases.english: Floods from the sea also come together with an earthquake.
after it comes a sheer mountain of water, piled high

phrases.latin: Sī mare subitō recesserit, in loca superiōra fugiendum est.
phrases.english: If the sea suddenly goes out, you must run to higher ground.

sources: Lewis & Short: inundatio · Lewis & Short: mons
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. tsunami, tidal wave, storm surge.
